one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is Microsoft's FY27 Q1 (September quarter) report. No event page is posted yet, but the pattern (Wed Oct 29 2025, Wed Oct 30 2024) points to Oct 28 or 29, 2026, before the Oct 30 scoring close. Guidance is revenue of $89.85-90.95B, Agents and Infra $75.15-75.75B, Devices and Consumer $14.7-15.2B, Azure +44-45% cc on the new definition, Windows OEM down low-twenties, and capex over $50B. Value-chain reads into the print are positive and point to capacity-limited demand: Nvidia hyperscaler revenue more than doubled with a $108B guide, AWS +37%, Google Cloud +82%, Oracle RPO $664B. On the Windows OEM side, the low-twenties decline is already guided and fits IDC's Q4 CY26 -20% PC call, so it should not surprise. The Oct 28 FOMC is also in the window. After the Sep 30 PCE print, swap-implied hike odds fell to about 36% (supervisor, citing Bloomberg), which is smaller macro drag than feared, and the Sep 30 close already reflects it. The OpenAI funding talks at about $1.4T (Sep 29) support the stake's value and ease the counterparty risk on the $250B Azure commitment. They are already public, though. The print will likely be judged on capex and RPO mix more than EPS. Net: I leave the round-1 1-month ladder unchanged: roughly symmetric, a slight positive tilt (median ~$521), and ~9.5% monthly vol (vs 32%/3.5 = 9.1%) because an earnings print falls in the window.

fair_value.method: Forward P/E on my own bottom-up EPS, with the OpenAI stake added separately. 60%: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of ~$23.9 x 23x core + $27 stake = $577. 40%: FY28 EPS of ~$23.0 (3% below consensus) x 22x + $27 = $533. Blended, about $559.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 guide of ~$15B/quarter annualizes to ~$60B. IDC sees the memory shortage lasting through end-2027 (Q4 CY26 -20%), and Gartner has 2026 units -10.4% with prices high through 2027. Windows OEM therefore stays weak through FY28, and search/gaming only offset it. I assume no FY28 recovery.

FY27 follows the 44-45% Q1 guide, easing through the year. For FY28 I start from the peer growth range (AWS 37%, Google Cloud 82% from a smaller base), industry backlogs (Oracle $664B, Google $514B) and Nvidia's hyperscaler guide, all of which say demand stays above supply into 2027. I then deduct ~3-4 pts for OpenAI's any-cloud right. Azure's $250B commitment is only about a third of OpenAI's ~$750B planned compute through 2030; Oracle ($300B from 2027) and AWS ($38B + expansion) take the rest. So OpenAI's incremental growth mostly goes elsewhere, while the committed $250B stays in RPO. Ex-OpenAI RPO growth of 25% sets the floor.
M365 commercial cloud is guided at ~+17% cc and the July-2026 M365 price rise adds to that. On-prem server and other lines grow slower, so I blend to ~10%.
Azure $196B + non-Azure A&I $205B + D&C $60B. To reach consensus Azure would need ~38% FY28 growth.

$23.68 x (1 - 1.3% revenue shortfall) x (1 - ~1.5% margin drag). Management guides FY27 operating margin down <1pt and the building useful-life change helps little. FY27 capex grows year on year beyond the CY26 ~$175B (which excludes ~$15B moved to operating leases), and $329B of uncommenced leases add fixed cost from FY27.
Today's price less a ~$27 stake is ~$491, over NTM EPS of ~$20.7, which is ~23.7x. I trim slightly because FY27 capex grows (not the $175B I assumed in round 1) and FCF yield is <2%.
~25% as-converted (10-K) x midpoint of $852B (March round) and ~$1.4T (Sep 29 talks) = ~$280B, less a 30% tax/illiquidity haircut = ~$196B, over ~7.43B shares = ~$26-27. No IPO in 2026.
A 1-turn discount to the core NTM multiple, for OpenAI concentration (~40% of $678B RPO, $24.1B = 7.3% of FY26 revenue) and the shift of OpenAI's incremental compute to Oracle and AWS.

bear.story: AI capex digestion. OpenAI's incremental compute goes to Oracle and AWS, and non-OpenAI demand fills new capacity slowly, so FY28 Azure growth drops to ~25%. The memory-driven PC slump keeps D&C shrinking. Depreciation and the $329B lease stack squeeze margins, FY28 EPS lands near $21, the core multiple falls to ~17.5x, and the stake is marked down (~$20).

base.story: Azure stays capacity-limited at ~42% in FY27 and ~35% in FY28. M365 pricing and Copilot carry Productivity, and D&C is flat at ~$60B. FY28 EPS is ~$23 (slightly below consensus), the core multiple is ~23x NTM, and the OpenAI stake is worth ~$27/share.

bull.story: The value chain keeps surprising upward (Nvidia and hyperscaler backlogs). Ex-OpenAI RPO converts fast, Copilot and agent monetization inflects, estimates rise 10%+, the multiple moves to ~27x, and the OpenAI stake is marked near $1.4T+ (~$40+/share).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$410 (about 21% down, ~17.8x my FY28 EPS of $23.0 ex-stake), the market would be pricing a real break in the AI-cloud thesis, not normal volatility. That means Azure growth well below guidance (under ~30%), stalled conversion of ex-OpenAI RPO, OpenAI failing to fund or scaling back its $250B commitment, or chain-wide overcapacity signs such as Nvidia or Oracle guidance cuts or lease cancellations. The ~$1.4T OpenAI raise makes the funding-failure path less likely.

reasoning: Round 2, industry lane. The supervisor established several facts I now use. (1) The ~$175B is calendar-2026 capex, and FY27 capex grows year on year, so capital intensity is higher than I assumed. (2) Microsoft holds ~25% of OpenAI as-converted, and OpenAI is raising at ~$1.4T, so I now add a ~$27/share net stake explicitly. (3) OpenAI is ~40% of RPO and all sequential RPO growth was non-frontier. (4) Following the supervisor's advice not to adopt consensus EPS, I rebuilt FY28 revenue bottom-up from industry evidence. Azure: FY26 $101.9B. FY27 is +42% per the Q1 guide and the peer demand signals (Nvidia, AWS 37%, Google Cloud 82%, Oracle RPO $664B). FY28 is +35%: capacity demand persists, but OpenAI's any-cloud right (April 2026) and its ~$750B compute plan, of which Azure's $250B is only about a third, mean OpenAI's incremental growth mostly goes to Oracle and AWS, costing Azure ~3-4 pts. D&C: ~$60B, flat in FY28, because IDC and Gartner see the memory shortage and high PC prices lasting through 2027. Result: FY28 revenue ~$461B, 1.3% below consensus. With ~1.5% margin drag from depreciation and leases, FY28 EPS is ~$23.0 (-3%). Valuation: the core P/E of 22-23x plus the stake gives ~$559 (round 1: $565). The lower EPS and the higher capex outweigh the explicit stake value. Scenarios: $395/21%, $560/54%, $715/25% (mean ~$564). The ladder uses a mix of lognormals with median ~$545-550 and a fat left tail. P(>= $518) moves 0.575 -> 0.565. Research was kept tight (5 queries this round). I no longer rely on the tech-insider.org AWS-OpenAI piece (graded low by the supervisor); the any-cloud right now rests on Microsoft's blog and the Yahoo report on OpenAI's compute plan. The consensus figures remain a single-aggregator input, used only as a reference.
